structured.answer: From what I read, a deposit locks the money until the agreed date for a fixed (or changing) interest, about 1.8% in their Leumi example. The bank takes 15% tax off the interest, and if I take the money out early the bank charges a fine and the page doesn't say how much. The thing that worried me most is it says there's no deposit insurance in Israel and a plain deposit doesn't keep up with rising prices, so I won't change anything yet. I'll ask you and the clerk about the penalty and about that insurance.

stuck.why: It showed 'ההפקדות שלכם 70,000 ₪' but 'נשאר לכם 68,270 ₪'. I didn't understand why a safe deposit leaves me with less than I put in. I only guessed it was because of 'בכסף של היום' and the 2% inflation.
'דמי יציאה ... לפי התעריפון של הגורם המציע' gives no number, so I still don't know what breaking the deposit costs.
'פטור למעוט הכנסה' with 69,840 ₪ and 10,920 ₪. I couldn't tell if it applies to me and Avi.
